name: Credit spreads
summary: US high-yield spreads 3.44%, inside the 4% Watch line but at a 52-week high
state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.44% on 30 Oct, inside the 4% Watch line but at its widest in a year and 20bp wider over the month. Lenders are demanding a little more for default risk as rates and energy costs stay high, but there is no broad credit squeeze.
for_you: Companies can still borrow on normal terms; no broad corporate credit squeeze is under way.

sources.title: FRED — ICE BofA US High Yield OAS

why: High-yield spreads show how much lenders demand to fund weaker companies — an early warning of defaults and credit crunches.
drivers: Default expectations, risk appetite, rates, private-credit stress, fund outflows.

rubric.alert: HY OAS > 6.0%, or widened > 200bp in a month.
rubric.watch: HY OAS 4.0–6.0%, or widened > 100bp in a month.
